executiveSummary: Amstelveen's GM0362 identity, generalized 2025 boundary, 95,822 population, 47 CBS neighbourhoods, one active BAG woonplaats, four BRT settlement polygons and Amsterdam-Amstelland safety-region membership are coherent. The complete ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service deterministic contract passes, including exact zero-intensity behavior, causal closure, bounded state, local reconciliation and map-layer invariance. The audit is nevertheless correction-required because the named Rhine, Meuse and IJssel preset assigns Amstelveen sustained direct inundation stress solely from a synthetic 50 km line-distance field. The official regional reference case describes a Lek/Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal pathway and names affected municipalities and Amsterdam areas, but not Amstelveen; Amstelveen's directly documented water mechanisms are high groundwater, pluvial loading, polder drainage, the Amstel and regional water defenses. A conservative interim exclusion is appropriate pending authoritative LIWO/AGV scenario geometry. Coastal, pluvial, wind, heat/drought, winter, remote Groningen-earthquake, wildfire/smoke and cyber outputs are bounded planning scenarios but not locally calibrated forecasts. First-72-hour operations also omit the Middelpolder pumping system, RWZI Amstelveen, current A9 construction restrictions and the nighttime cross-boundary acute-care dependency. All utility flows remain correctly labeled logical transfer proxies; unavailable physical topology, crews, backup, inventory and restoration data are not inferred.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 — filtered municipality row GM0362
supports: Official GM0362 population 95,822, density 2,331 per square kilometre, age-65-plus count 18,649 and one-person-household count 20,139.
Reference totals for checking generated municipality and rounded neighbourhood statistics.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek
evidenceSources.title: Gemeente gegeneraliseerd 2025
supports: Official GM0362 code, Amstelveen name and generalized administrative geometry used by the application.
Boundary-edition and municipality label-point checks; related CBS neighbourhood, BAG woonplaats and safety-region collections retain their separate provenance.

evidenceSources.title: Plan voor Energietransitie, Circulaire economie en Klimaatadaptatie 7.0 (PLECK 7.0)
supports: Amstelveen identifies alternating wetter and drier periods, its clayey soil, groundwater management, water storage, wadis and heat-stress reduction as local adaptation priorities.
The municipality is conducting new regional heat and water-overload stress tests in 2026; these results are intended to support the climate-adaptation plan from 2027.
Heat measures target people over 75, young children and people with vulnerable health; drinking-water tap and cool-place actions are local context rather than simulator inventories.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028 — detailed risk inventory and analysis
supports: The official reference river case is a Lek breach/high-water wave through the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal; its stated affected locations include Diemen, Ouder-Amstel and Aalsmeer but do not include Amstelveen.

A polder or regional-dike failure is more probable than a sea or major-river flood; extreme rain can exceed polder and sewer-pump capacity and drought can threaten peat dikes, foundations, water quality and supply.

The Amsterdamse Bos is about 1,000 hectares but regional nature-fire risk is assessed as small; there is no gas extraction in the region and earthquake probability is assessed as very small with limited impact.

Electricity, gas, drinking water, wastewater, telecom, food and transport disruptions have cascading effects; Liander, PWN and Waternet are named at regional level, including interconnection between PWN and Waternet supplies.
Cyber disruption, severe storm, heat and extreme precipitation are regional risks; nearby Schiphol and dense cross-boundary mobility are important context.

evidenceSources.title: Gemaal Middelpolder
supports: The Middelpolder pumping station lies in Amstelveen and pumps the polder to the Amstel to maintain a habitable water level.
The published capacity is 300 cubic metres per minute; the structure and pump installation require renovation or replacement and are remotely operated.

evidenceSources.title: Onze plannen voor 2026 — gezond water en gezuiverd rioolwater
supports: RWZI Amstelveen is an operating named wastewater-treatment dependency receiving investment in 2026.
The water authority is improving wastewater-treatment automation and security against cyberattack, directly connecting drainage and cyber continuity.

evidenceSources.title: Verbreding A9 — current works, closures and diversions
supports: The A9 through Amstelveen is an active construction corridor with a 1.6 kilometre sunken section and staged traffic arrangements through 2029.
At the audit date the Keizer Karelweg on-ramp is closed until February 2027, with additional local closures and September 2026 full-weekend closures and diversions published.

evidenceSources.title: Naar de huisarts of het ziekenhuis? — current acute-care routing
supports: Ziekenhuis Amstelland's emergency department accepts referred acute patients from 08:00 to 22:00; at night non-announced emergency care is directed to Amsterdam UMC.

The out-of-hours GP post serves Amstelveen and surrounding municipalities, while after 23:00 the night pharmacy is at OLVG West in Amsterdam, establishing time-dependent cross-boundary care dependencies.

identity.summary: GM0362, Amstelveen, Noord-Holland and Amsterdam-Amstelland are internally and officially coherent.
notes: The generated feature id, municipality bundle code and name all equal GM0362/Amstelveen.
The generated safety-region overlay contains GM0362 in exactly one region: Amsterdam-Amstelland.
The current Kadaster bestuurlijke-gebieden endpoint independently returns identification GM0362, name Amstelveen and province Noord-Holland.

geography.summary: The generated 2025 generalized boundary and centre point are coherent, with distinct source editions kept visible.
notes: The generated centre [4.851913537833831, 52.28660331069974] is inside the official generalized municipality geometry.
Both boundaryEdition and statisticsEdition are 2025; newer Kadaster definitive geometry was used only as an independent identity reference and did not silently replace the generated boundary.
BAG woonplaats, BRT settlement and CBS municipality/neighbourhood geometries are different ontologies and must not be expected to have identical edges or totals.

demography.summary: Core municipality statistics match CBS 2025 and rounded neighbourhood totals reconcile closely.
notes: Generated municipality population 95,822 and density 2,331 exactly match the filtered CBS row.
Generated age65Pct 19.5 is the rounded share implied by CBS age-65-plus count 18,649; generated one-person households 20,139 exactly match CBS.

The 47 published neighbourhood rows sum to population 95,825, only 3 above the municipality row (0.003%); age-65-plus rows sum to 18,665 and one-person households to 20,115 because CBS publishes rounded local counts.

regionalDetail.summary: All 47 official neighbourhoods expose the 36-field schema and reconcile, but several CBS fields are suppressed or unavailable and must remain null.
notes: Population, age, household, business, car, land, water and address-density fields are available in all 47 neighbourhoods.
Home-value coverage is 44/47, cars-per-household 41/47, social-assistance 45/47, doctor and supermarket distance 46/47; no unavailable value is coerced to zero.
District-heating percentage and public-charging-point count are null for all 47 neighbourhoods in the consumed CBS edition.

The bundle contains 45,910 households, 14,120 establishments, 7,073 non-residential buildings, 39,095 cars, 4,111 hectares land and 297 hectares water; these are aggregate allocation context, not operational asset inventories.

No neighbourhood has zero published residents; Stadshart has the largest establishment count (855) and is inspectably the highest activity allocation weight for all eight services in the compound T+24 detail.

settlements.summary: One BAG woonplaats and four BRT settlement polygons are correctly retained as distinct products.
notes: The active BAG woonplaats is Amstelveen and its label centre is not outside the generalized municipality boundary.
BRT supplies Amstelveen, Bovenkerk, De Zwarte Kat and Nes aan de Amstel: two woonkernen, one deelkern and one buurtschap.
The BRT settlement-population sum 97,120 is 1,298 above the CBS municipality total and is correctly treated only as cartographic context, never as a replacement population total.

transport.summary: The seven NWB-derived boundary links are coherent logical routes, but current works and multimodal operational capacity are not represented.
notes: Consumed links are two A9 trunk links, N522, two N231 links and two N201 links, with five neighbouring municipality codes; every endpoint resolves.
No ProRail station geometry lies inside GM0362, while 118 scheduled-transit stop areas are present. This does not mean Amstelveen lacks tram or bus dependency.

At no-event T+0 each of the seven links has health 1 for all eight service views and each service sees nominal logical capacity 1,270; E07 documents current and scheduled access restrictions that are not ingested.
NWB geometry and GTFS stop context do not establish emergency throughput, live availability, vehicle capacity, detours or the cross-boundary acute-care route in E08.

emergencyContext.summary: Official local sources establish polder, wastewater, heat, transport, acute-care and cascading-infrastructure dependencies absent from the generic model.
notes: The detailed VrAA source is the governing regional risk context; it distinguishes sea, major-river and more probable polder/regional-dike mechanisms rather than treating one proximity scalar as hydraulics.
Middelpolder pumping and RWZI Amstelveen are concrete local drainage dependencies; their control, backup, staffing and failure states are not public model inputs.
A9 works and time-dependent local versus Amsterdam acute care materially affect a real first-72-hour plan.
No sensitive utility topology, operator restoration promise, emergency stock, crew, fuel or facility backup state was inferred from public descriptions.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at T+0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 for all eight services.
notes: Peak municipality severities were storm 0.601572, pluvial 0.393824, river 0.116578, coastal 0.356080, heat 0.716414, winter 0.630445, cyber 0.551447, earthquake 0.019882, wildfire 0.109202 and compound 0.901207.
At T+24 the compound frame had rain 49.523799 mm/h, inundation amplitude 0.391482, wind 28.751267 m/s, cyber disruption 0.483784, system pressure 0.590081 and 60,762 modeled residents under pressure.

At T+72 the compound frame retained inundation amplitude 0.391482 and cyber disruption 0.062921, with system pressure 0.608806, 63,290 modeled residents under pressure and 3,487,745 cumulative event-attributable person-hours.
apps/web/src/scenarios.ts is a thin clone of the canonical sim-core presets, so the audited configurations equal the user-selectable scenarios.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, monotonic burden, exact no-event semantics, determinism and municipality/local reconciliation pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0362 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services.
Every canonical preset with intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable person-hours at all checkpoints.
Compound T+24 local detail reconciled population 95,822 and affected population 60,762 exactly for every service; demand and delivered totals reconciled with maximum floating error 3.56e-14.

Repeated T+24 frames were byte-deterministic, service demand and delivery remained finite and bounded, cumulative person-hours were monotonic and all route flows remained bounded by effective logical capacity.
Changing among all 11 map layers left the compound T+24 physical hazard, municipality pressure and affected population exactly unchanged.

spatialPlausibility.summary: One direct major-river result is unsupported, and the remaining local hazard fields are screening scenarios rather than source-specific spatial models.
notes: The river preset emits 0.370190 internal inundation amplitude at both T+24 and T+72, system pressure 0.171961/0.181259 and 4,315/5,570 people under pressure even though E04's named Lek pathway does not identify Amstelveen among affected locations.

The local river pattern ranks Betsy Perkbuurt, Boekenbuurt and Schrijversbuurt highest because of deterministic seeds, not elevation, dike compartments, Amstel hydraulics, pumps or LIWO arrival/depth grids.

Coastal T+24 emits 1.345099 internal amplitude, system pressure 0.481501 and 46,103 people under pressure. A regional sea-breach scenario is plausible, but this value has no named breach, probability class, connected footprint, arrival time or source-specific depth semantics.
Pluvial loading is locally plausible given E03–E05, but density plus seed cannot locate documented groundwater, storage, sewer, catchment or pump constraints.

Storm, heat/drought and winter hazards are regionally plausible per E03/E04 but are synthetic preset forcing, not observations or a KNMI warning. The Groningen-earthquake preset is remote and low; wildfire produces zero direct flame but 0.258333 smoke severity at T+24, while a local Amsterdamse-Bos event would require an explicit epicentre and fuel/spread data.
Cyber is a relevant regional cascade but its untargeted municipality severity is seeded rather than based on an incident, asset or threat assessment.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service states are computed and balanced, but local assets and operators are not represented as physical dependencies.
notes: Compound T+24 availability by service was power 0.256498, water 0.414489, drainage 0.401949, gas 0.632379, telecom 0.313406, mobility 0.412550, facilities 0.546557 and supply 0.407280.

E04 identifies Liander electricity/gas context and coupled PWN/Waternet drinking-water resilience, but all power, water, gas and telecom transfers in the simulator reuse the same seven NWB road links.
Drainage has no explicit Middelpolder pump or RWZI Amstelveen node despite E05/E06; facilities have no Ziekenhuis Amstelland schedule or nighttime Amsterdam UMC/OLVG dependency despite E08.
Mobility has no live A9 construction state, and supply has no supermarket, pharmacy, depot, vehicle, visitor/worker, household stock or last-mile inventory.
The model correctly exposes every road-derived intermunicipal flow as transferSemantics logical-proxy and does not claim it is utility topology.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality ledgers close and identify scenario assumptions, dependencies and counterfactuals without upgrading evidence confidence.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; service contributions plus baseline sum to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, driver metadata, recovery progress and service-restoration counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
The system-pressure weights cover all eight services, and household preparedness affects modeled people/supply after physical pressure rather than changing hazard fragility.
Operational-control and intervention effects are labeled scenario assumptions, while utility corridors are labeled logical proxies.

recovery72h.summary: Recovery guards behave consistently, but no public local restoration or resource data calibrates the 72-hour trajectories.
notes: River forcing remains active at T+72 and all eight service recovery-progress values remain exactly zero, avoiding a false all-clear during modeled standing water.

At T+72 the ended coastal forcing retains system pressure 0.176738, 4,959 people under pressure and service recovery progress 0.485071–0.930294; this is synthetic damage/recovery, not an operator estimate.
Compound standing water blocks generic restoration at T+72; seven services retain their T+24 availability and facilities decline from 0.546557 to 0.412806 through modeled dependencies.
Actual pump/RWZI state, A9 restrictions, acute-care routing, crews, fuel, spares, mutual aid, backup runtime and operator restoration estimates are unavailable and therefore unverified.

findings.summary: A synthetic proximity corridor creates unsupported direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel inundation in Amstelveen.
findings.evidence: E04's detailed official river reference is a Lek breach/high-water wave through the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal and names Diemen, Ouder-Amstel, Aalsmeer and specified Amsterdam areas as affected, not Amstelveen. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts riverExposure() instead measures GM0362's centre to three coarse line segments and returns a positive value whenever distance is at most 50 km. The canonical river frame consequently reports internal inundation amplitude 0.370190 at T+24 and T+72, 4,315 then 5,570 modeled people under pressure, and zero recovery while the forcing remains active. This is a shared deterministic field defect exposed by GM0362, not evidence that every Amstel/polder pathway is safe.
findings.action: As a conservative interim safety screen, add GM0362 to the explicit direct major-river exclusion in riverExposure(), with a regression asserting zero direct river inundation at all six checkpoints while indirect network effects remain possible. The durable correction is to replace municipal code exclusions and diagonal proximity lines with an approved, named LIWO/AGV Lek, boezem or dike-breach scenario mask including source, probability class, arrival, coverage and uncertainty. Do not reclassify Amstel/polder or pluvial failure as Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing.

findings.summary: Coastal, pluvial and neighbourhood flood allocation lacks Amstelveen's hydraulic compartments and named scenario evidence.
findings.evidence: E03–E05 distinguish clay/groundwater stress, urban storage, regional dikes, the Amstel and actively pumped polders. The model instead combines municipality density, coastline/river distance and deterministic neighbourhood seeds. Coastal T+24 produces internal amplitude 1.345099 and 46,103 modeled people under pressure without a breach or connected flood footprint; the river local rank puts Betsy Perkbuurt first without elevation or dike evidence. The UI correctly calls the generic value inundation stress, but its spatial allocation is not validated depth or arrival.
findings.action: Ingest only approved LIWO/AGV breach, regional-water and pluvial layers; retain separate coast, Lek, Amstel/boezem, polder and cloudburst mechanisms. Show the selected source/scenario, probability class, spatial resolution, arrival and uncertainty, and do not display metres unless the selected layer is a calibrated depth product.

findings.summary: The drainage layer omits the Middelpolder pumping and RWZI Amstelveen dependencies.
findings.evidence: E05 identifies a 300 m³/min remotely operated Middelpolder station that maintains the polder level and is due for renovation; E06 identifies RWZI Amstelveen and 2026 automation/cyber-security work. Yet drainage availability is generated from generic hazard, power, cyber and road-derived transfer terms: 0.462179 in pluvial T+24 and 0.401949 in compound T+24, with no pump, catchment, sewer or treatment node in its dependency chain.
findings.action: Add public, non-sensitive water-system asset classes and relationships for polder pumping and wastewater treatment, with independently configurable state, power/control dependency, catchment coverage and operator-sourced recovery assumptions. Keep exact controls, security and backup unknown unless approved by AGV.

findings.summary: Static NWB links omit current A9 construction access restrictions and scheduled full closures.
findings.evidence: E07, updated 31 August 2026, documents the ongoing A9 sunken-alignment work, the Keizer Karelweg on-ramp closure through February 2027, other local restrictions and September full-weekend closures/diversions. The no-event T+0 model gives both A9 boundary links health 1 and nominal capacity 260, and each service receives the same seven-route capacity sum 1,270. These are disclosed logical values but cannot support a current first-72-hour access claim.
findings.action: Introduce a dated, modal operational-status overlay separate from immutable NWB geometry. Preserve source, validity interval, direction, ramp/through-route distinction and diversion; show explicit stale/unavailable state when no current feed exists. Do not hard-code temporary 2026 works into permanent road geometry.

findings.summary: A municipality facilities scalar hides time-dependent cross-boundary acute-care and pharmacy routing.
findings.evidence: E08 states that Ziekenhuis Amstelland's emergency department is available for referred acute care from 08:00 to 22:00, non-announced nighttime emergency care is directed to Amsterdam UMC, and the post-23:00 night pharmacy is at OLVG West. The simulator gives one facilities availability per municipality and has no facility, opening-hours, referral, bed/staff, pharmacy or cross-boundary care node, so it cannot explain whether the real night pathway remains reachable during A9 or service disruption.
findings.action: Represent public facility roles and hours separately from aggregate availability, then model explicit cross-boundary referral edges and transport dependencies. Keep capacity, staff, generator fuel and continuity agreements unknown until operator-verified.

findings.summary: Power, water, gas, telecom and supply flows are logical road-corridor proxies, not Amstelveen utility topology.
findings.evidence: E04 names real regional operators and states that PWN and Waternet networks are interconnected, but does not publish the physical topology or emergency state required for simulation. The model reuses exactly seven NWB links, health 1 and logical capacity sum 1,270 for every one of the eight service views. All emitted routes correctly carry transferSemantics logical-proxy and the UI fidelity badge says logical service transfers, preventing a false physical-network claim.
findings.action: Retain the disclaimer and do not infer substations, pipes, pressure zones, telecom exchanges, critical customers or stock routes. Replace each layer only with independently licensed and operator-approved topology, capacity, dependency, backup and restoration inputs.

findings.summary: Wind, heat/drought, cloudburst and winter values are plausible stress tests but lack local event calibration.
findings.evidence: E03 and E04 establish local/regional relevance for high groundwater and heavy rain, heat, drought, strong wind, cold, snow and ice. The model's peaks—storm 0.601572, pluvial 0.393824, heat 0.716414 and winter 0.630445—come from preset intensity, season, density and deterministic seed, not a dated KNMI observation/forecast or Amstelveen 2026 stress-test layer. Boundedness is therefore not validation of physical magnitude or neighbourhood rank.
findings.action: Keep scenario labeling and add optional timestamped KNMI observations/warnings and approved municipal stress-test layers with provenance and uncertainty. Preserve the synthetic presets for exercises and never describe them as forecasts or return periods.

findings.summary: The remote Groningen earthquake result is small and bounded but not a local seismic hazard assessment.
findings.evidence: E04 states there is no gas extraction in Amsterdam-Amstelland and assesses earthquake probability as very small with limited impact. The canonical Groningen epicentre yields peak severity 0.019882 in GM0362 and zero current shaking by T+24, while cumulative event-attributable burden remains 24,120 person-hours at T+24 and 39,578 at T+72 through synthetic damage/recovery. The preset has no occurrence probability or event-specific KNMI ShakeMap.
findings.action: Retain explicit Groningen-event naming and scenario confidence. For any real event, use an event-specific KNMI ShakeMap/validated ground-motion model and local site/asset vulnerability; do not infer probability from the displayed stress.

findings.summary: Remote wildfire flame screening is conservative, but local Amsterdamse-Bos fire and smoke behavior are uncalibrated.
findings.evidence: E04 identifies the approximately 1,000-hectare Amsterdamse Bos while rating regional nature-fire risk as small. The default remote wildfire at T+24 produces direct flame intensity exactly zero in GM0362, smoke 0.258333 and drought 0.479464, which respects the finite flame footprint but is not dispersion or exposure science. A local epicentre can be selected, yet the model still lacks land cover, fuels, moisture, wind-aware spread, suppression and fire-water state.
findings.action: Keep direct flame and smoke separate. Require an explicit local incident/epicentre and add authoritative fuel/land-cover, weather and response inputs before using a neighbourhood fire footprint operationally.

findings.summary: Official identity, rounded demography and service-specific activity allocation are inspectably coherent.
findings.evidence: E01/E02 agree with GM0362 identity and headline totals. All 47 neighbourhoods retain official nulls, population differs from the municipality row by only 3, and local compound T+24 allocation reconciles municipality population, affected people, demand and delivery across every service. Stadshart's 855 establishments and 659 non-residential buildings contribute to the highest activity weight without inventing extra residents or criticality.
findings.action: Retain source editions, null semantics, reconciliation tests and the explicit distinction between resident population and non-residential activity.

findings.summary: The current deterministic, causal, zero-intensity and recovery safety contracts pass for GM0362.
findings.evidence: The focused audit gate passed all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Exact zero intensity clears event severity, peak, affected population and event-attributable person-hours; route semantics remain logical-proxy; contribution and counterfactual arithmetic closes; T+24 repeats exactly; layer selection cannot change physics; sustained modeled water blocks generic recovery at T+72. A headless Chromium check selected Amstelveen/river/T+72, exercised all 11 layers, displayed 25% inundation stress and the logical-service-transfer fidelity badge, and produced no console or page errors.
findings.action: Keep these invariants in the national gate when correcting GM0362-RIVER-001 and adding source-specific local dependencies.

corrections.summary: Conservatively remove unsupported direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing from GM0362 pending source-specific hydraulic geometry.
corrections.validation: Add GM0362 to the interim audited exclusion and assert river-flood flood stress is exactly zero at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 while indirect service/network effects remain allowed. Then run pnpm test, MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0362 pnpm audit:model and MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=ALL pnpm audit:model. Preferred machine source: the public LIWO GeoServer OWS at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows with catalogue/API metadata at https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2; ingest approved scenario identifiers, footprints and arrival/depth products, never a synthetic river corridor. LIWO publishes release versions rather than a fixed cadence (the inspected public configuration identifies application 2025.1.6 and dataset 2025_0_1); its public landing/configuration does not declare a reuse licence, so preserve source-layer terms, version and retrieval time and require licence review before redistribution. The successor test must use an approved LIWO/AGV scenario fixture and assert only its connected footprint receives direct water.

corrections.summary: Add source-specific Amstelveen polder, drainage and wastewater dependencies without exposing sensitive controls.
corrections.validation: With approved AGV fixtures, distinguish pluvial, Amstel/boezem, polder and primary-water scenarios; represent Middelpolder pump and RWZI Amstelveen as public asset classes with power/control dependencies; verify spatial coverage and failure/recovery provenance; never expose or infer security-sensitive topology. Preferred public machine sources: PDOK Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA WFS https://service.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-kunstwerken-imwa/wfs/v2_0?SERVICE=WFS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities for gemaal features (CC BY-SA 4.0, weekly), PDOK Waterbeheergebieden IMWA OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterbeheergebieden-imwa/ogc/v1 for polder/peil/flow areas (CC BY-SA 4.0, weekly), and PDOK Waterketen DAMO OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 for RWZI/rioolgemaal public assets (CC BY-SA 4.0; provider cadence is published as unknown and contributor completeness varies). Record provider, object identifier, dataset timestamp and licence in every derived snapshot; use synthetic topology only when a dependency is genuinely unavailable or security-sensitive and label it explicitly.

corrections.summary: Separate immutable road geometry from dated modal operational restrictions around the A9.
corrections.validation: At an audit-date 2026-09-02 fixture, show the Keizer Karelweg ramp restriction without declaring the entire A9 closed; at the published September weekend fixture, apply direction/mode-specific closure and diversion; outside validity intervals fall back to explicit unknown/static geometry rather than persisting a stale closure. Preferred public machine source: NDW DATEX II v3 complete/planning and live situation feeds documented at https://docs.ndw.nu/handleidingen/NCIS/WebportaalD2v3/ and available through https://opendata.ndw.nu/ or the authenticated pull endpoint https://backbone.ndw.nu/pull/datex3-complete. NDW updates records on change; its pull guidance recommends 60-second polling, and NDW website/open-data content is CC0 unless a product states otherwise. Persist situation/version/validity timestamps, archive an audit snapshot, and supplement—not replace—the feed with the dated official Amstelveen/Rijkswaterstaat works notice E07.

corrections.summary: Represent public acute-care roles, hours and cross-boundary referral paths independently from generic facilities availability.
corrections.validation: Test weekday/weekend/holiday and local-clock boundaries around 08:00, 22:00 and 23:00. A nighttime Amstelveen case must expose the Amsterdam UMC and OLVG West routing assumptions and mobility dependency without inventing beds, staff, acceptance, generator runtime or response-time guarantees. Preferred machine sources: the RIVM 2025 SEH/acute-obstetrics workbook at https://data.rivm.nl/meta/srv/api/records/0c25694e-3b4c-41a2-bf89-6b88ecda23cc/attachments/Antwoorden%20vragenlijst%202025%20tbv%20data.rivm.nl.xlsx.zip (public domain; annual survey) for declared acute-care roles, and BAG OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/kadaster/bag/ogc/v2 (Public Domain Mark 1.0; daily) for authoritative addresses/geometry. Exact local hours, nighttime referrals and pharmacy routing have no identified authoritative machine feed, so curate them from the official hospital page E08 with retrieval/effective dates and a scheduled freshness check; do not synthesize operational capacity.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic stress-test prototype, not a KNMI forecast, warning, return-period estimate, current incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved LIWO/AGV breach, arrival, depth, flow, catchment or polder-compartment layer is ingested; generic inundation amplitude is not a measured water depth.

The official detailed river reference's omission of Amstelveen supports a conservative direct-effect exclusion, not a claim that all indirect Lek, Amstel, boezem or network consequences are impossible.
CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve parcels, buildings, elevation, basements, dikes, sewers, pumps, households, workers, visitors or individual vulnerability.
The municipality's refreshed 2026 heat and water-overload stress-test results are not yet consumed or treated as public calibration.

No physical Liander, PWN, Waternet, gas, telecom, drainage, hospital or emergency-supply topology, live state, priority-customer list, controls, crews, fuel, spares or restoration forecast is available to the model.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse NWB-derived logical corridors and must not be interpreted as utility pipes, cables, telecom links, hospital transfers or food routes.
Static NWB and GTFS inputs do not establish live construction, closures, detours, schedules, vehicles, emergency throughput or accessibility.
Facility and supply layers lack verified beds, staff, patient acceptance, care-home occupancy, pharmacy/supermarket stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.
Wildfire lacks local fuels, ignition, moisture, spread, dispersion, suppression and fire-water data; earthquake lacks event probability and local site/asset response.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls, not observed Amstelveen resources or commitments.

Six-hour audit checkpoints can miss short cloudbursts, shaking, dispatch, road works and schedule transitions; the first-72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
Rounded CBS fields, incomplete local coverage and distinct BAG/BRT/CBS reference dates prevent false exact reconciliation across products.
provinceReviewFlags: Review every Noord-Holland municipality receiving direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel stress from the shared 50 km proximity field against the relevant safety-region reference pathway and approved LIWO geometry; preserve indirect effects separately.
